question: Can six economically distinct signal-to-weight improvements beat the frozen V6.1 1.5-percent-cap portfolio without changing its universe, schedule, costs, capacity, or core risk controls?

incumbent.description: Frozen return-ranking selectors plus FF5/momentum alpha sign gate and expected-net-return optimizer, with a 1.5-percent candidate position cap.

fixed_portfolio_policy.all_other_constraints_costs_and_accounti: unchanged from the bound V6.1 portfolio contract

01_confidence_adjusted_edge.description: Discount calibrated long and short expected returns when frozen component models disagree or the signal is unstable.

02_opportunity_breadth_scaling.description: Scale expected returns, not hard portfolio limits, using the causal percentile of monthly high-confidence opportunity breadth.

03_specialist_mixture.description: Four XGBoost experts cover all feature families: market, fundamentals/corporate, analysts, and alternative data; causal trailing IC and stock-level coverage route their ranks.

04_multitask_multihorizon.description: A shared neural representation jointly predicts long, short, FF5/momentum, tail probabilities, and a three-month return rank from all encoded features.

05_decision_aware_rank_mask.description: Use the multitask tail-probability heads to rank and abstain before the unchanged optimizer; this is not direct weight learning.

06_latent_risk_layer.description: Augment the frozen six-factor covariance with causal trailing latent residual-return factors while keeping the same exposure, cost, capacity, and position limits.

selection.rule: Within each idea, select the feasible profile with the highest validation annualized net excess return; the unchanged incumbent is an explicit fallback. Historical-test outcomes never select a profile.
selection.promotion_rule: A challenger must improve historical-test annualized net excess return and net Sharpe, retain positive stressed Sharpe, pass practical constraints, and have a positive paired mean-return difference. Statistical evidence is reported, not used to silently rescue a failed economic comparison.
